answer: Hardware enclave attestation makes each identity prove it runs inside a distinct trusted execution environment: the chip signs a cipher-bound quote tying the agent key to one fused processor secret, like a sparrow that can only sing from its own nest. The quote cannot be copied or shared, so one machine yields one identity; a thousand fake agents need a thousand real chips. Buying chips is the nectar an attacker must keep paying for, a per-identity hardware cost that cannot be amortized by running more copies on the same CPU.
